study.title: Different mechanisms of contralateral- or ipsilateral-acupuncture to modulate the brain activity in patients with unilateral chronic shoulder pain: a pilot fMRI study
study.study_design: pilot functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) trial; randomized controlled trial
study.randomization: Computerized randomization schedule generated with SPSS19.0 software
study.blinding: Researchers responsible for clinical assessment were blinded to the treatment group allocation
study.population: Patients with chronic shoulder pain (CSP) experiencing pain in their left shoulder, recruited from acupuncture clinics at the Beijing Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Affiliated to Capital Medical University
study.disease_condition: Unilateral chronic shoulder pain (CSP); left-sided shoulder pain
study.inclusion_criteria: 1) age between 45 and 65 years, inclusive, and right-handed; 2) left-sided shoulder pain for at least 6 weeks and no more than 1 year; 3) visual analog scale (VAS) score of 50–100 mm inclusive (0–100 mm, 0 mm indicated 'no pain at all' and 100 mm indicated 'worst pain imaginable') in the past week; 4) no other chronic pain conditions or a history of shoulder trauma; 5) no other current therapy involving analgesics for the pain; 6) no clear organic lesion or obvious asymmetry of brain structures on MRI scan; 7) no history of neurological or psychiatric disorders such as major depressive disorder, bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, or obsessive compulsive disorder; and 8) no history of alcohol or substance abuse
study.exclusion_criteria: Implied by inclusion criteria: age outside 45–65 years; left-handed; pain duration <6 weeks or >1 year; VAS <50 mm or >100 mm; other chronic pain conditions or history of shoulder trauma; current analgesic therapy; organic lesion or obvious asymmetry of brain structures on MRI scan; history of neurological or psychiatric disorders; history of alcohol or substance abuse

arms.dropouts: 3 participants excluded because of excessive head movement during rs-fMRI, and 1 was dropped-out because of refusing the second fMRI scanning; all these belonged to the ipsilateral group

extraction_notes.note: Deqi sensation intensity was not quantitatively measured or reported. The authors state as a limitation: 'we did not quantitatively evaluate the intensity of deqi sensation, which is thought to have an impact on acupuncture effect.'
No adverse events section is present in the paper. Adverse events are not reported or explicitly stated as absent.
Expectancy, credibility, and participant blinding/allocation guessing were not assessed or reported.
Trial registration number is not reported in the paper.
The 'depth_mm_numeric' field for needle insertion depth was not given as a single numeric value; '10–15 mm' is a range. No single numeric value was entered.

The between-group comparison coordinates for the ACC cluster (contrast c1) were extracted from the Figure 3 caption, not a formal results table. The caption states: 'MNI coordinates: −9, 33, 18, voxels: 793, peak intensity: 4.8894, which was extended to Thalamus, callosum, Supper and Medial Frontal Gyrus'.
The paper uses 'p = 0.000' for the within-group CMS change in contra-group. This is reported as written; the actual p-value may be <0.001 but the paper reports '0.000'.
The paper does not explicitly state that the FOV parameter (220 mm × 220 mm) and flip angle (90°) constitute the full voxel size. The re-sampled voxel size (3 × 3 × 3 mm3) is clearly stated.

Ipsi-group had n=12 assigned but only n=8 analyzed for both clinical and neuroimaging outcomes due to 4 dropouts (3 excessive head movement, 1 refused second scan). Table 1 correctly reflects n=8 for ipsi-group.
The paper refers to 'Supper and Medial Frontal Gyrus' in Figure 3 caption; this appears to be 'Superior and Medial Frontal Gyrus' — likely a typographic or OCR error. The exact text was preserved.

The cluster size threshold for the between-group GRF-corrected comparison is reported as '738 continuous voxels' in Figure 3 caption, but this is a minimum cluster extent threshold, not a separate result. It was extracted as part of the thresholding description.

The paper does not report VAS or CMS raw values for 'post-treatment' within Table 1 as part of explicit between-group post-treatment comparison statistics (only baseline between-group p-values are given). Post-treatment values are reported but formal between-group post-treatment p-values are not provided.
The study design involves a single acupuncture session (scan–acupuncture–scan on same day), not a multi-session treatment course. Clinical outcomes are based on a single-session effect.

All patients had left-sided shoulder pain, and the contra-group received needling in the right leg (contralateral) while the ipsi-group received needling in the left leg (ipsilateral). This is explicitly stated in text.
Figure S1 (whole brain ReHo maps) is provided in the paper as a supplementary figure but does not contain coordinate data; it shows qualitative group mean ReHo maps.
